text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing to the group multiplies value but individually keeping tokens is the dominant strategy since each contributed token only returns 0.3 to me versus 1.2 to the whole group. Mathematically, free-riding maximizes individual payoff, but full cooperation would maximize total welfare—so I need to decide whether to play purely rational or lean cooperative across the 10 rounds.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game: the multiplier makes group contribution socially efficient but individually costly, so keeping tokens is the dominant strategy while full cooperation yields the highest collective payoff of 24 per round each.

Since we only see group totals, not individual contributions, conditional strategies are hard to sustain across 10 rounds. I'll open with a moderate contribution, say 10, as a signal rather than going all-in or all-out.

I'm weighing whether a modest contribution might help sustain group cooperation going forward.
